headline: Split by position and reconnect the two chains
statement: Reorder a singly linked list so nodes in odd positions come first, followed by nodes in even positions. Positions start at one; this concerns position, not the parity of node values. Keep the original relative order in both groups and reuse the original nodes.
intuition: Maintain tails for the odd and even position chains. Each tail skips the next node in its current chain to reach the next node of the same positional parity. Save the even head to reconnect after the final odd node.
approach: Return immediately for an empty list.
Track odd at head, even at head.next, and save even_head.
Advance odd and even links by two while an odd successor exists, then join odd.next to even_head.
correctness: After each iteration, the odd chain and even chain contain the corresponding processed positional groups in original order. Rewiring appends exactly the next same-parity node. Once every node is processed, joining the chains gives the required stable order.
bruteForce: Store odd and even nodes in separate arrays and reconnect them, using O(n) extra space.

complexity.explanation: Every node is rewired at most once; only three pointers are stored.

pitfalls: Group by node position, not value.
Save the even head before moving the even pointer.
The final chain must remain acyclic and contain every original node once.
